notes:
Account background:
- FalconForge Media: global adtech platform (DSP + personalization). Heavy real-time inference load for creative selection and reranking.
- Previously evaluated OpenAI and Anthropic hosted APIs; primary blocker was cost and noisy tail latency under burst traffic.
Sales / technical timeline:
- 2026-02-15: Intro call (Maya) — talked high-level goals. Customer asked about dedicated pools, predictable token economics.
- 2026-02-25: Product demo + console walk-through (Liam) — showed per-route telemetry and cost breakdowns. Customer liked rollout policies.
- 2026-02-28: Deep technical call (SE + infra) — recorded (ff_call_2026-02-28_6632). Discussed traffic shapes and SLOs.
- 2026-03-04: Security & legal intake — provided SOC2 attestation and initial security FAQ. Legal requested SLA language for latency credits.
- 2026-03-10: Pre-workshop alignment — customer committed to share 7-day QPS histogram and 30 sample prompts for model eval.
Workshop objective (what customer asked for):
- Run a dedicated capacity sizing workshop focused on: baseline QPS, tokens/sec per request, steady-state vs peak planning, throughput guarantees, and SLA latency bands (p50/p95/p99).
Customer traffic profile (from initial telemetry):
- Steady-state baseline: ~60 QPS of inference requests across two routes (rerank & personalization).
- Average request tokens (prompt + expected completion): 600 tokens (400 prompt, 200 completion).
- Peak bursts seen in events: spikes to ~420 QPS sustained for 3–5 minutes during campaign launches.
- Percentiles matter: 60% of requests are short (<=200 tokens), 30% mid (200–800), 10% long (>800).
Preliminary sizing assumptions (workshop inputs / Redwood draft):
- Target latency SLOs desired by FalconForge: p50 <= 50ms, p95 <= 150ms, p99 <= 300ms (for rerank/short-path; personalization can accept slightly higher).
- Desired throughput guarantee: 99.5% of requests meet SLOs under steady-state; burst handling with graceful degradation and fallback model variants for tails.
- Performance model (based on Redwood kernels + A100-class GPU): approximate sustained token/sec per GPU = 1.2M tokens/sec for mixed-length workload with dynamic batching and KV-cache on typical retrieval flows.
- Baseline reserved pool recommendation (initial): 4 x A100-80GB equivalent GPUs dedicated to low-latency/short-path traffic (reranking, personalization), plus 2 x A100 reserved for long-running generation tasks; autoscale burst pool of 2 GPUs.
- Expected steady-state capacity with 4 GPUs: ~4.8M tokens/sec capacity -> maps to ~120 QPS at 600 tokens/request with comfortable headroom (x3 multiplier applied for safe burst headroom).
- Peak handling plan: primary pool handles steady-state; burst pool + autoscale (2 GPUs) expected to cover spikes to ~420 QPS with small increase in p95 (~180–220ms) — fallback to smaller quantized model for tail if SLO violated.
- Cost/ARR impact: draft shows dedicated commitment (~12 months) in the 200k–350k ARR band depending on reserved burst options and model family.
SLA negotiation points to prepare for workshop:
- Define measurable latency SLOs per route (rerank vs personalization) and per-token accounting (how tokens measured for billing).
- Uptime target for Dedicated control plane vs inference plane; requested 99.95% inference availability.
- Credits model for p99 latency SLO misses during agreed steady-state windows (how many minutes/days tolerated).
- Data residency carve-outs for EU bidders; need clear deployment mapping.
Technical asks from customer ahead of workshop (items they will share):
- 7-day traffic histogram (minute granularity preferred).
- 30 representative prompts per route + expected payload sizes.
- Current SLA language they have with other vendors (for negotiation leverage).
Workshop deliverables Redwood will produce:
- Baseline QPS -> GPU sizing worksheet (per-route breakdown), simple simulator that converts token/sec -> expected latency curves under config knobs (batch size, max gen length, kv cache hit rate).
- Cost model: estimated monthly committed spend + burst costs and unit token pricing for the proposed pool.
- SLA term sheet draft: proposed latency SLOs, availability, and credit calculation for review by FalconForge legal.
- POC plan: 4-week pilot (1 dedicated pool + traffic replay) with success criteria: p95 < 150ms under peak-simulated load, no more than 2% error increase vs hosted baseline.
Open risks / blockers (expanded):
- Legal needs tighter language on latency credits — they asked for p99 credits rather than p95; internal legal wants clear formulas.
- Engineering must validate quantized model quality for creative generation (QA needed).
- Budget: procurement prefers a phased commitment; finance requesting a mid-point ARR estimate before signing.
Notes / rep shorthand and next follow-ups:
- Customer vocal about predictability and unit economics ("We need not just speed but cost tail visibility").
- SE to prepare a short simulator notebook and 2 candidate model variants (full and quantized) to demo during workshop.
- Next meeting: 2-hour sizing workshop week of 2026-03-16; Maya to confirm calendar by 2026-03-13.
- Redwood deliverable due: preliminary sizing + cost by 2026-03-19.
